claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on the present record, provided the unresolved enterprise refund-policy summarization limitation is explicitly disclosed, and that the current evidence supports certification more than a claim that no material weakness remains.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the required limitation disclosure has been incorporated into the final model card or release artifact.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A final model card or equivalent launch artifact explicitly disclosing the enterprise refund-policy summarization limitation.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.

concern_ledger.concern: No approved mitigation or risk acceptance is in evidence; the runbook remains draft with TBD fields.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Approved mitigation or risk-acceptance documentation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Without approved mitigation satisfying policy predicates, draft monitoring cannot remove the current disclosure requirement or support a clean certification posture.

concern_ledger.concern: The recommended action label certify_model overstates what the evidence supports unless it is explicitly conditioned on disclosure.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Launch approval language or actor output that expressly conditions certification on the required disclosure, plus evidence that the disclosure is in place.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The admissible record supports at most a conditional certification path, not an unqualified conclusion that certification is presently cleanly supported.

decision_criteria: A compliant certification needs either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation/risk acceptance satisfying the policy predicates.
If a named launch use-case limitation remains unresolved, the record must show explicit disclosure before certification can be treated as compliant.
Draft monitoring or rollback concepts can support risk management but do not substitute for finalized approval or disclosure.
Actor framing cannot convert a conditional rationale into unconditional support when the admissible record still shows an open limitation.
evidence_requests: Final model card or release artifact showing the enterprise refund-policy summarization limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Materiality determination for the unresolved refund-workflow issue if the actor contends disclosure is not required.
Final launch approval record showing certification is conditioned on the disclosed limitation rather than a clean no-limitations representation.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence confirms an unresolved below-target named launch slice in enterprise refund-policy summarization.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The mitigation artifact is only a draft and is missing a finalized rollback threshold and review date, so it does not qualify as an approved mitigation that removes the disclosure requirement.
The current model-card draft reportedly says there are no known material limitations, which conflicts with the unresolved slice issue unless the card is updated before certification.
The recommended action is stated as certify_model, but the evidence only supports certification conditioned on explicit limitation disclosure, not unconditional certification.
unsupported_claims: There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has already been made or approved in final form.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Any interpretation of the current record as showing no remaining material weakness in every named launch slice is unsupported.
